english: It's not true that both Kim and Lee passed. Kim passed, so Lee didn't.
Neither Kim nor Lee passed, so it's not true that they both passed.
Kim and Lee didn't both pass, so neither of them passed.
note: The scope slip models make most: 'didn't both' is ¬(X∧Y), not ¬X∧¬Y

english: It isn't true that the café or the bookshop is open, so the bookshop isn't open.
If the milk smells, it isn't fresh. This milk is fresh, so it doesn't smell.
The plant won't grow unless it gets sunlight. It isn't getting any sunlight, so it won't grow.
If the heater isn't on and the window is open, the room gets cold. The heater isn't on. The window is open. So the room will get cold.
note: The ¬ covers only the heater, not the whole antecedent

english: The door is locked if and only if the light isn't blinking. The light is blinking, so the door isn't locked.
If neither Max nor Ruby ate the cake, the dog did. Max didn't eat the cake, so the dog ate it.
